build: Official update records through the post-launch patch and Blood Price update
observations: Official patches changed attack buffering so dash could occur between strikes and improved buffering after dash-strikes.
A patch fixed dash invulnerability that persisted after cancellation into an attack.
Official updates revised dash-related visual effects, hit effects, reward presentation, and chamber layouts.
A patch made selected gaps easier to cross reliably and clarified cover in a boss chamber.
inferences: Movement feel depends on transition rules between locomotion, offense, protection, and animation—not dash speed alone.
Level geometry and feedback require revision alongside controller timing when movement reliability changes.
limits: Patch notes establish changed behavior but do not publish the complete state machine or timing values.
This record does not claim one cancellation model fits every combat system.
